name: Lemon Quartz
physical: Crystal healers link it to digestion and vitality
Many people keep it nearby for energy during long workdays
summary: Lemon Quartz is a pale, greenish-yellow quartz of mental clarity, optimism and bright focus, favored in crystal healing for study, work and fresh starts.
intro: Lemon quartz is quartz with a cool, greenish-yellow tint, like the pale rind of a lemon, rather than the amber glow of citrine. Almost all of it is created by heating or irradiating colorless or smoky quartz, then cutting it into faceted gems that have a bright, clean sparkle. Some trade names, such as Oro Verde or green gold quartz, are used for the more intense greenish stones. It is usually affordable and often used in jewelry that needs a fresh pop of color. For crystal lovers, it is a light, springy stone that feels like a sunny window.
history: Lemon quartz has no traditional ancient lore of its own, because the color arose largely from modern treatment methods. Heat and radiation treatment of quartz developed in the 20th century, with Brazilian mines supplying much of the rough. The stone was soon cut into gems and sold under names such as lemon citrine or oro verde. Its name speaks plainly to its look. Because older cultures prized yellow stones as symbols of the sun, many of those associations were carried over to lemon quartz by modern practitioners, who treat it as a bright cousin to citrine.
meaning: Lemon quartz is a stone of mental clarity and cheerful energy in crystal tradition. Practitioners link it to the solar plexus chakra and say its fresh color wakes up the mind without overheating it. It is popular with students, writers and anyone facing a long to-do list. Emotionally it is associated with optimism, a lighter mood and a willingness to try again. It is often recommended for clearing mental clutter and for beginning projects with a clean slate. Spiritual workers use it to brighten meditation and encourage playful curiosity. Gently, it is connected to vitality, digestion and a sense of lively energy, in the symbolic way yellow stones have long been viewed.
howToUse: Place a faceted lemon quartz on your desk in a sunny spot to refresh your workspace. Hold it for a minute before studying to set a focused intention. Wear it as a pendant near your solar plexus on days that need extra brightness. Add it to a grid for new projects with clear quartz in the center. Put a tumbled stone in your bag during exams or interviews. Meditate with it while picturing a bright, lemony light filling your chest and head, then set it on a windowsill to catch the day.
care: Lemon quartz is durable and handles water, so a quick rinse in cool water is fine. Keep treated stones out of very strong, prolonged sunlight, as some irradiated or heat-treated material can fade over time. Cleanse with moonlight, smoke, sound or a selenite plate. Dry with a soft cloth and store it in a pouch away from harder gems. Avoid sudden temperature changes and ultrasonic cleaners if the stone has visible fractures.
identify: Lemon quartz is nearly always treated, so look for a clean, slightly greenish yellow with little natural zoning. Natural citrine tends to be more orange or honey colored. Glass imitations show bubbles and a warmer feel in the hand. Synthetic quartz can be made in lab-grown yellow, so ask the seller. Stones sold as natural lemon quartz are rare, and the treatment does not harm the stone or its durability. A refractometer or a gemologist can confirm quartz.

faq.q: What is lemon quartz good for?
faq.a: Lemon quartz is traditionally used for mental clarity, optimism and focus. Crystal healers link it to the solar plexus and recommend it for study, creative work and getting started on new projects.

faq.q: Is lemon quartz the same as citrine?
faq.a: They are related but not identical. Both are quartz, but lemon quartz is a cooler, greenish yellow and is almost always treated, while citrine tends toward honey and orange tones.
Some treated stones can lighten after long exposure to strong sunlight or heat. Keep it out of hot cars and blazing windows, and charge it with moonlight if you want to be safe.
